mcp-abap-adt/search.semantic: Find the ABAP short dumps (runtime errors, crashes) of a program, a user or a time range; also system messages and SAP Gateway errors.

description: [read-only] Reads one page of the runtime feed named by feed_type in one request, newest first: the ABAP short dumps (runtime errors) of the user, object_name or time range from–to given, or system messages or SAP Gateway errors. Optional: feed_type(dumps|system_messages|gateway_errors, default dumps), user, runtime_error, exception, object_name, package, component, top (1 to 100), from, to. Response: JSON { feed_type, count, entries, next_to }; each dump carries dump_id; next_to is the `to` of SAP's next link, present when more remain. The next link's page starts at the boundary second, inclusive: entries of that second may repeat; match them by dump_id. Runs on an ABAP session of its own. Optional timeout (seconds): when it passes, the read is cancelled, its ABAP session logged off, and the system stays as it was. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a client's cancel ends only the client's wait, and SAP runs the read on. Recordable: in batch mode a call is recorded under the next number and answers with empty content; its answer is read by number after the batch ends.

component.description: Dumps whose application component contains this text, in any case.

exception.description: Dumps whose exception class contains this text, in any case.

feed_type.description: Which runtime feed to list. Default "dumps" (ABAP short dumps). "system_messages" and "gateway_errors" read the other two ADT runtime feeds through the same call.

object_name.description: Dumps whose terminated object name contains this text, in any case.

package.description: Dumps whose object package contains this text, in any case.

runtime_error.description: Dumps whose runtime error contains this text, in any case.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the answer: a whole number, at least 1, no default — without it the call waits until SAP answers. When it passes, the read is cancelled (its ABAP session is logged off) and the call answers that nothing was changed. Set it below your MCP client's request limit — the TypeScript SDK's client cancels at 60 s; a cancel does nothing to SAP.

to.description: End of time range (YYYYMMDDHHMMSS), inclusive: the page holds the entries up to that second; a previous answer's next_to is the next page's to, and that page starts at the boundary second, inclusive.

top.description: Entries the page holds, 1 to 100 (SAP answers 100 when top is absent).

name: HandlerDumpList
